deployer: A five-broker South Florida boutique that markets self-storage and small flex assets; the agent drafts BOV pricing, buyer-financing talking points and offering-memorandum tables for the brokers.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Normalize a seller T-12 into broker NOI and test it against the asking cap rate
Show a buyer what a lender will actually fund (DSCR vs LTV vs debt yield)
Produce a defensible price and cap-rate table for a BOV or OM
hardest_task: A seller hands over a 78,000 NRSF Hialeah self-storage T-12 claiming $1.12M NOI and wants a $19.5M ask (5.74% cap). The agent must spread the T-12, normalize for a 4% management fee and a Florida tax reassessment on sale, then show what debt a buyer can raise at 6.75% / 25 years and the buyer's five-year levered IRR, so the broker can defend or reset the price before the first buyer call.
data_it_needs: Self-storage line items (fee income, tenant protection plans, truck rental) in the chart of accounts
Miami-Dade assessed value and millage for the post-sale tax estimate
Sold storage comps with cap rates
Same-store street-rate and occupancy trends
dealbreakers: Any number it cannot reproduce in Excel
Silent guesses on unmapped lines
Outputs with no formula or source to cite to a buyer
budget_note: Brokerage tech spend is tight and per-seat; will pay only for something a buyer's analyst can re-run, and has no budget for a tool that cannot see Florida data.

deployer: A national tenant-representation brokerage whose copilot, built in Microsoft Copilot Studio, helps its industrial advisors compare landlord proposals and prepare client decision memos.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
top_tasks: Rank three to six landlord proposals for a 150,000-500,000 SF logistics requirement on one effective-cost basis
Renew-versus-relocate analysis for an existing client occupancy
Pull market lease comps with verified terms for a negotiation
hardest_task: A 3PL client needs 250,000 SF of distribution space from March 2027 and has three landlord proposals in different markets with different terms (84 versus 120 months), free rent (4 to 6 months), TI ($2 to $5/SF), bump structures (percent versus fixed $/SF) and expense structures (NNN at $2.60-2.80/SF with 3% growth versus a gross deal). The agent must put them on one discounted effective cost per SF per year at 7.5%, then test renewing the current 250,000 SF at $8.40/SF versus moving, including moving cost, downtime and double rent, before the advisor sends the client a memo.
data_it_needs: Verified industrial lease comps (rent, free rent, TI, term, expense basis) by submarket
Landlord proposal terms extracted from PDFs
A tenant-side net effective cost that includes NNN expenses and growth
Citable formula and steps for a client committee
dealbreakers: A ranking the advisor cannot reproduce in Excel
Silent acceptance of obviously wrong units
A tool that cannot be wired into Copilot Studio or Gemini without engineering help
budget_note: Enterprise procurement buys through IT security review, so a free hosted endpoint is a pilot only; a firm like this would need SSO or OAuth and a data-handling statement before production.

deployer: A four-person Dallas owner-operator and asset manager that holds three mixed-use buildings (ground-floor retail, upper-floor office) and runs a Gemini/Copilot-based assistant for its two asset managers and its bookkeeper.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
incumbent_tools: an outside tax consultant for protests
top_tasks: Year-end CAM reconciliation for mixed retail and office tenants with different caps, base years and admin fees
Property-tax protest calendar and deadline tracking for each building
Percentage-rent and lease-expiration monitoring for the ground-floor retail
hardest_task: A 48,000 RSF mixed-use building averaged 78% occupancy in 2026 against 95% gross-up clauses. Five tenants have five different structures: a bakery with a 5% compounding cap off a 2024 base and a 10% admin fee after the cap, a salon that excludes marketing, two office tenants on a base year ($560,000) and an expense stop ($480,000), and a studio that moved in July 1. The agent must reconcile them all from an $893,000 expense pool with a $140,000 roof replacement excluded, and the asset manager must also know the protest deadline before the 2027 notices arrive.
data_it_needs: Dallas CAD notice dates and assessed values per account
Verified deadline logic for ARB protests
Lease clause extraction for caps, exclusions and gross-up so the inputs are right
Dallas parcel and owner facts to cross-check the tax bill
dealbreakers: A reconciliation whose order of operations it cannot trace line by line
A deadline rule that is wrong or unverified
Anything that requires its small team to host software
budget_note: Cost-sensitive: spends on tools only when they replace a tax-consultant or bookkeeper hour; a $49 plan is fine if it saves one afternoon a year-end.

role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: The commercial real estate credit group of a Midwest regional bank, whose Copilot Studio agent drafts sizing grids, refinance tests and payoff estimates for credit officers.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
incumbent_tools: Moody's CRE / Trepp-style CMBS data (a subscription)
top_tasks: Size a loan across LTV, DSCR and debt yield with a stress grid
Test whether a maturing loan can be refinanced and what the payoff and prepayment cost is
Produce an amortization schedule and balloon for the term sheet
hardest_task: A 612-bed purpose-built student housing property near a Missouri campus has underwritten NOI of $3.85M and a $52M appraisal. The bank prices at 6.40%, 30-year amortization, 65% LTV, 1.35x DSCR and 9% debt yield, and wants stress cases (NOI down 10-15%, rate up 100 bp, value down 10%), a refinance test against a $31.5M maturing loan with yield maintenance at Treasury 4.10% plus 50 bp, and a 10-year schedule with 24 months interest-only on actual/360.
data_it_needs: Per-bed rent roll and lease-up data for student housing (pre-leasing, academic-year terms)
CMBS loan-level comparables and watchlist status
Verified formulas it can cite in a credit memo
County parcel and recorded mortgage data for the collateral
dealbreakers: A sizing result that cannot be reproduced in the bank's own model
Unstated day-count or discounting conventions
Any tool that stores or logs borrower financials without a clear statement
budget_note: A bank buys through vendor risk management; a $49 plan is not the issue, an unattested hosted service is. Would use the open-source local server first to avoid sending borrower data out.

role: Corporate occupier and real estate portfolio agent
deployer: The real estate department of a Carolinas grocery chain (about 140 stores, most leased in grocery-anchored centers), whose Custom GPT helps three analysts with lease accounting, lease-vs-buy and renewals.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
incumbent_tools: a lease administration system (CoStar-style or Yardi-style)
top_tasks: Remeasure operating leases for extensions and option exercises under ASC 842
Lease-versus-own analysis for new store sites
Portfolio WALT and renewal-cliff tracking
hardest_task: A Raleigh store lease is extended on 2027-01-01: 12 months remain at $62,000 a month and a five-year extension at $68,500 a month is agreed, so 72 payments, in advance, at a new 5.8% incremental borrowing rate. The analyst needs the new liability, the ROU asset, the straight-line lease cost and the journal-ready schedule, then a lease-versus-own comparison for a 52,000 SF store with 15-year horizon before the real estate committee.
data_it_needs: ASC 842 remeasurement with a cent-exact schedule
Lease vs own with debt and residual
WALT across the store portfolio
Rules and parcel facts in North Carolina counties
dealbreakers: A Custom GPT import that fails or truncates operations
Numbers the controller's team cannot tie to its lease accounting system
Any operation the GPT cannot see because of the 30-operation limit
budget_note: Has corporate budget, but a Custom GPT is an internal convenience; the controller owns lease accounting, so it needs auditability more than price.

role: Property management, operations and CAM agent
deployer: A Seattle third-party property manager with about 30 mid-market assets, mostly mixed-use buildings with ground-floor retail under apartments, using Claude Code in the operations team to script monthly and year-end reports.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
top_tasks: Year-end CAM reconciliations for ground-floor retail tenants across the portfolio
Monthly apartment rent roll analysis: GPR, loss to lease, concessions, occupancy, expirations
Percentage-rent billing for retail tenants and owner reporting
hardest_task: One 8-unit sample of a 65-unit apartment-over-retail building: the monthly rent roll needs GPR, vacancy, model and down units, loss to lease and amortised concessions (two weeks free, a month free, a $500 credit), and the retail side needs a batch CAM reconciliation with a gross-up from 60% to 100% occupancy and 15% admin fees that bill more than the pool. The plugin skills claim their worked examples were checked against the live API.
data_it_needs: Rent roll metrics that tie to Yardi exports
CAM reconciliation with every clause-driven setting visible
Percentage rent breakpoints (natural and fixed)
Seattle and King County building-performance rules (CBPS, BEPS)
dealbreakers: Worked examples in the docs that do not reproduce
Silent unit errors (annual rent entered as monthly)
Anything that forces the team to leave Claude Code
budget_note: Per-property management fees are thin; the firm pays for tools that remove an analyst day per quarter. Free hosted tier is fine; data-leaves-machine needs owner consent.

deployer: A Tampa-based mid-market retail investor that buys grocery-anchored neighborhood centers in Florida for a value-add fund; the agent supports three underwriters with lease abstraction, rent-roll DCFs and exclusive-use diligence.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
incumbent_tools: a lease-abstract template maintained by a paralegal
top_tasks: Abstract an anchor lease (term, rent steps, exclusives, co-tenancy, go-dark, radius) and tie every term to a page and quote
Check proposed shop-space uses against the anchor's exclusives and prohibited uses
Rent-roll DCF with a rollover blend and an exit cap, against the asking price
hardest_task: A 66,000 SF grocery-anchored center near Orlando (48,000 SF anchor at $14.50 on 10 years left, two shops at $28 and $32) is offered at $19.5M. The underwriter must abstract the anchor lease with page-and-quote citations (including exclusive use with carve-outs, co-tenancy at 70% of GLA, a 90-day go-dark recapture and a 5-mile radius), check a proposed butcher shop against the exclusive, and run a five-year DCF at an 8% discount rate and 6.75% forward exit cap to see if the price works.
data_it_needs: Lease clause extraction that cannot invent a quote
Exclusive-use conflict screening against the anchor lease
A DCF whose conventions are stated so they can be compared with ARGUS
Florida parcel, owner and sales data for comp-checking the seller's narrative
dealbreakers: A tool that confidently passes a misquoted clause
DCF conventions that differ silently from ARGUS
Fabricated or unverifiable citations
budget_note: Already pays for ARGUS and CoStar, so FactLot has to be a free addition or a clear time-saver; will not pay for hosted registry regions that are not open.

deployer: A mid-market Austin investor that buys mixed-use properties (ground-floor retail with office or apartments above) in Central Texas; an in-house Python agent builds underwriting packages and JV waterfalls for the investment committee.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
incumbent_tools: an internal Python package for waterfalls
top_tasks: Direct-cap valuation with below-the-line adjustments against the asking price
JV equity waterfall (pref, tiers, residual promote) for the investment committee
Lease comp intake and net effective rent for retail suites
hardest_task: A 98,000 SF mixed-use asset in South Austin is offered at $23.5M against forward NOI of $1.48M. The agent must value it by direct cap at 6.25% with a $60,000 reserve, $310,000 lease-up cost, $95,000 free-rent burn-off and $420,000 of deferred maintenance, then run the JV waterfall (90/10 LP/GP, 8% compounding pref, 12% and 16% hurdles at 20% and 30% promote, 40% residual) on a five-year $12M equity raise, and log a retail comp in a shareable format.
data_it_needs: Deterministic valuation and waterfall math with conventions disclosed
A comp format and validator for sharing lease comps
Travis and Bexar county parcel, owner and sales facts
Texas protest dates tied to the property
dealbreakers: Fields silently ignored (typos in JSON keys)
Conventions that differ from the operating agreement without a warning
Needing a human to translate a vendor error message
budget_note: In-house engineering time is the cost; will adopt a free API that replaces hand-built waterfall code, would pay modestly for a key if rate limits or SLAs matter at scale.

role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: A two-person family investment office in Ohio that owns six small-bay industrial and flex buildings in secondary markets and runs a LangGraph agent for deal screening and exchange planning.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
top_tasks: Track 1031 exchange deadlines and test identification and boot
Screen small-bay industrial acquisitions by cap rate, DSCR and price per SF
Size debt for a replacement property
hardest_task: The family sold a 24,000 SF small-bay building in Dayton on 2026-10-20 for $3.2M ($160,000 expenses, $1.1M debt relieved, $900,000 basis). It must identify replacement properties by 2026-12-04, close by the earlier of 180 days or the tax return date, and buy a $3.4M replacement with $900,000 of new debt and $40,000 of costs without creating mortgage boot. The agent should do the date math, the identification tests and the boot netting, and say plainly that it is not tax advice.
data_it_needs: Exact 45- and 180-day dates and days remaining
Identification-rule checks (three-property, 200%, 95%)
Boot, debt replacement and recognised gain
Small-market comps (Ohio, Indiana, Michigan) for screening
dealbreakers: A tool that gives tax advice or implies an exchange qualifies
MCP wiring that needs custom session handling
Context cost that makes a small agent too slow or expensive
budget_note: Two people, no technology budget beyond model API costs; a free hosted endpoint is the point, and $49 is justified only if it saves an accountant or QI call.

deployer: The multifamily valuation group of a national appraisal firm's Atlanta office; its Claude-based assistant drafts income-approach workups and checks rent-roll and cap-rate arithmetic for the signing appraisers.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Rent roll analysis: GPR, loss to lease, concessions, physical and economic occupancy
Income approach: direct capitalization across a cap-rate range, rounded as appraisers report
Ten-year DCF cross-check and implied IRR against a comp sale price
hardest_task: A 60-unit Atlanta garden property (four floor plans, 57,450 SF) has a rent roll with 47 occupied, 2 on notice, 6 vacant, 2 model and 3 down units, concessions on a third of the leases, and an as-of date of 2026-11-01. The agent must produce GPR, loss to lease, concessions and economic occupancy, build a stabilized NOI of about $770,575 (93% stabilized collections, $78,000 other income, $583,000 of expenses plus a 3% management fee), capitalize it at 5.25%, 5.50% and 5.75% with a $15,000 reserve and $120,000 of lease-up cost, round to $100,000, and cross-check with a ten-year DCF at 7% and a 6% terminal cap.
data_it_needs: Rent roll metrics that tie to the client's roll
Cap-rate indications from sales (CoStar / market data)
Fulton and DeKalb County parcel and assessment records
Stated conventions so every figure can go in an appraisal report workfile
dealbreakers: Numbers the appraiser cannot reproduce in the workfile
A tool that presents itself as appraisal advice
Silent changes in conventions (timing, rounding)
budget_note: The firm buys data subscriptions per office; a tool that checks arithmetic and documents steps could be adopted on an innovation budget, but the signing appraiser carries the liability, so it must be an aid, not a source.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: A New York real estate boutique law practice that runs buyer-side diligence on multifamily and mixed-use acquisitions; a Custom GPT built on ChatGPT Enterprise helps paralegals abstract leases and check estoppels.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Abstract ground-floor commercial leases and amendments with citations and current-state precedence
Compare tenant estoppels with the lease and rent roll
Cross-check ACRIS deeds, mortgages and BBLs and building-emissions exposure (LL97)
hardest_task: A 90-unit West Side multifamily building has a ground-floor commercial lease (2,100 RSF, $68/RSF stepping, $75,000 security deposit, expiring 2030) with a first amendment extending it to 2035 at $70 and $77. The paralegal needs a current-state abstract with page-and-quote citations and amendment precedence, then a comparison of the tenant's estoppel (which states a 2033 expiration, a $57,000 deposit, the old $68 rent and a termination option the lease lacks) against it, and BBL matching to ACRIS records.
data_it_needs: Quote-level citations a partner can check
Amendment precedence handled automatically
Estoppel-to-lease comparison
NYC BBL normalization and ACRIS deeds/mortgages (hosted lookups)
LL97 emissions exposure
dealbreakers: A hallucinated or unverifiable citation
Advice-like language that implies a legal conclusion
Data leaving the firm's control without a clear statement
budget_note: Billed hours drive adoption: pays for anything that cuts abstract time, but the firm's confidentiality duties mean it would prefer the local server, and a hosted service must state that documents are not stored.
